bib.title: Efficient Estimation of Word Representations in Vector Space

question: Can high-quality word vectors be learned from billions of words with much lower computational cost than neural network language models?
hypothesis: Removing the non-linear hidden layer gives simpler log-linear models that, trained on far more data, yield more accurate vectors for syntactic and semantic regularities.
contributions: Two log-linear architectures, CBOW and Skip-gram
A Semantic-Syntactic Word Relationship test set (8869 semantic, 10675 syntactic questions)
Comparison with NNLM, RNNLM and public vectors on accuracy and training cost
State of the art 58.9% on the Microsoft Sentence Completion Challenge with Skip-gram + RNNLMs

method.summary: CBOW (average of 4 past and 4 future words predicts the middle word) and Skip-gram (a word predicts words within a window, C=10) are trained with hierarchical softmax over a Huffman tree, SGD with Adagrad in DistBelief. Vectors are scored on word analogy questions by cosine nearest neighbour of vec(b)-vec(a)+vec(c).
method.task: word embedding learning, evaluated on word analogy and sentence completion

datasets.name: Google News corpus
datasets.preprocessing: vocabulary restricted to 1 million most frequent words; 30k for the subset experiments in Table 2

datasets.name: LDC corpora (as in Mikolov et al. 2011, ref 18)
Semantic-Syntactic Word Relationship test set
datasets.source: built by the authors; pairs listed manually, questions formed by connecting two pairs (e.g. 68 US cities gave about 2.5K questions)

datasets.name: MSR Word Relatedness (syntactic) test set of Mikolov et al. 2013

models.name: CBOW
models.architecture: log-linear, no hidden layer, shared projection, hierarchical softmax

other.Q: N x D + D x log2(V)

models.name: Skip-gram
models.architecture: log-linear, predicts words within range C before and after
models.context: C = 10, R sampled from 1..C per word

models.name: Feedforward NNLM
models.architecture: input, projection, hidden, output; hierarchical softmax

other.training: previously trained, about 8 weeks on a single CPU

training.objective: classify the middle word from context (CBOW) or surrounding words from the current word (Skip-gram), hierarchical softmax over a Huffman tree
training.optimizer: stochastic gradient descent with backpropagation; in DistBelief mini-batch asynchronous gradient descent with Adagrad
training.lr_schedule: linear decay to approach zero at end of last (Tables 2, 4) or only (later) epoch
training.epochs: 3 for Tables 2 and 4; 1 for later experiments
training.hardware: CPU only; 50 to 100 DistBelief model replicas, CPU cores an estimate (shared data center)
training.compute: Table 6: NNLM 14 x 180, CBOW 2 x 140, Skip-gram 2.5 x 125 [days x CPU cores]
training.wall_clock: CBOW about a day, Skip-gram about three days on a single CPU on a Google News subset

other.complexity: O = E x T x Q, E = 3-50, T up to one billion
other.skipgram_sampling: less weight on distant words by sampling fewer of them

inference.decoding: nearest word by cosine distance to vec(biggest)-vec(big)+vec(small); input question words discarded
inference.samples: not stated; single runs, no seeds

parameters.MSR sentence completion: 640-d Skip-gram; sentence score is the sum of predictions of surrounding words with the candidate at input; combined with RNNLMs by a weighted combination (weights not given)

metrics.name: analogy accuracy
metrics.definition: question correct only if nearest word equals the expected word exactly; synonyms count as mistakes

metrics.name: Sentence Completion accuracy
metrics.definition: pick the most coherent of five candidates

metrics.name: training time
metrics.definition: days, or days x CPU cores in DistBelief

availability.code: single-machine multi-threaded C++ code at code.google.com/p/word2vec (follow-up, section 7)
availability.weights: over 1.4 million named entity vectors trained on more than 100 billion words (follow-up)
availability.data: test set at www.fit.vutbr.cz/~imikolov/rnnlm/word-test.v1.txt; Google News corpus not stated as released

limits: Training corpus (Google News 6B) is internal; no variance or seeds reported.
Exact-match accuracy makes 100% unreachable; no morphology input.
Batch size, window beyond C=10, subsampling and negative sampling are not covered here (later paper 1310.4546).
Weights of the Skip-gram + RNNLM combination are not given.
Table 6 CPU core counts are estimates from shared machines.
The architectures are compared at different data sizes and dimensions in several tables, so not all rows are like for like.

terms.definition: continuous bag-of-words: log-linear classifier with four future and four history words at the input, predicting the middle word
classifies a word based on another word in the same sentence, predicting words within a range before and after
